{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Outsourcing Agreement (M&I / Tri City National Bank)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of the M&I Outsourcing Agreement — verified findings, deviations and next steps

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The overall picture is mixed but manageable: several of the provisions that most often cause trouble are already acceptable or better than our preferred position, while the risk is concentrated in the money-and-exit provisions.

**What is already in good shape.** The Vendor-side indemnity in § 14.2(B) is a genuine defend-and-indemnify obligation covering IP infringement, violation of protective laws and loss from M&I's acts or omissions, with no customer-modification carve-outs — at or above our preferred position. The Article 23 source-code licence covers our Affiliates automatically and our designees, and is not revocable at M&I's discretion. There is no non-compete, no MFN and no vendor audit right against us. Governing law and exclusive venue (Wisconsin / Milwaukee County) are our client's own home jurisdiction, so we would not move them. Renewal is by mutual agreement only, with a customer-side 12-month extension option. The § 16.1 warranties are not time-limited and are backed by service credits, cure-and-terminate rights and direct damages that expressly include re-procurement costs.

**Where the exposure sits.** The liability regime is the central problem: § 13.4 caps **only M&I's** liability, at **three months' fees**, below our six-month floor and with no carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality, data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP. That cap also cuts down the otherwise strong § 14 indemnity. Compounding this, § 13.5 deems the Termination for Convenience and Termination for Cause Fees to be **liquidated damages payable by us** and carves them out of the cap. Exit economics are punitive: an eight-year Term, a one-year convenience notice period, and a fee measured against the Estimated Remaining Value. Assignment is asymmetric (M&I may assign freely; our carve-out is narrow). There is no obligation on M&I to return Customer Data in machine-readable form or to certify deletion. Custom work we pay for is owned by M&I under § 10.4 "even if paid for by Customer", and §§ 8.1(ii) / 10.3(A) create a multi-year take-or-pay on the bundled Services. Insurance omits E&O and cyber/privacy cover for a vendor that hosts our customer data.

**Items requiring manual attention.** Three findings did not clear verification and must be worked by hand before we send anything: the exclusivity analysis (worker failure — no conclusion reached), and the proposed redlines for termination for convenience and for insurance.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 13 Damages (§ 13.4) | One-sided cap at three months' fees, no Excluded Claims carve-outs. Walk-away territory. Redline proposed. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 14 Insurance and Indemnity (§§ 14.2(B), 14.3) | At or above preferred on scope; no combination/modification exclusions. Note: § 13.4 cap would cut it down — addressed under LOL-CAP, not double-flagged. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 13 Damages (§ 13.5) | Termination fees deemed liquidated damages and carved out of the cap; fails fallback three-month limit. Redline proposed. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 22 Miscellaneous (§ 22.4) | M&I may "freely assign"; our carve-out limited to a merger into an Affiliate of a $100M-capital financial institution. Redline proposed. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Needs review** | — | Automated review failed (tool loop exceeded). No conclusion; manual review required. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 23 Source Code | Automatic Affiliate coverage, designee use permitted, not revocable at M&I's discretion. Noted only: licence runs to end of Term rather than perpetual. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 22 Miscellaneous (§ 22.14) | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction; only a mutual employee non-solicit (see NOSOLICIT). |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 22 Miscellaneous (§ 22.14) | All employees, whole Term, no carve-outs. Redline lands the clause at the fallback. |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 Termination (§ 11.1); § 10.2 | One year's notice plus a percentage of Estimated Remaining Value over an eight-year Term. Proposal drafted but **verification failed** — manual rework needed. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | Section reference not available in findings (§ 11.4 / § 17 discussed) | Six-month assistance limb is fine; no data return in machine-readable format within a fixed period and no certified deletion. Redline proposed. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 16.1 (By M&I) | Warranties untimed (exceeds preferred); disclaimer expressly subordinated to § 16.1; real remedies in §§ 9.2.D, 12.1, 12.3, 13.1. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 21.4 (Reliance on Data) | No vendor audit right against us; all examination rights run in our and our regulators' favour. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 22 Miscellaneous (§§ 22.1, 22.2) | Wisconsin / Milwaukee County — not on the enumerated list, but our client's home forum. Litigation, not arbitration. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 18 Management of Project | No MFN. § 18.4 is a right to bid and be considered only. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 2 Term (§ 2.2) | No auto-renewal; renewal by mutual agreement. Customer-side 12-month extension at then-current terms. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Deviation** | § 14 Insurance and Indemnity (§ 14.1) | No professional liability (E&O) and no cyber/privacy cover; CGL limits unstated. Proposal drafted but **verification failed** — manual rework needed. |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | Section reference not available in findings (§ 10.4 / § 17.2 discussed) | Custom work owned by M&I "even if paid for by Customer". Fallback redline: perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Developed Software. |
| Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | **Deviation** | § 10 Modification or Termination of Services (§§ 8.1(ii), 10.3(A), 10.2) | Multi-year take-or-pay on the bundled Services feeding the termination-fee formula; M&I may withdraw non-Core Services on 90 days' notice. Fallback redline proposed. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the points we should treat as conditions of signature rather than negotiating chips.

1. **§ 13.4 — three-month, Vendor-only liability cap (critical).** The cap is below our six-month floor, applies only to M&I (we are left uncapped) and has no carve-outs. It is squarely in walk-away territory and it also erodes the value of the § 14.2(B) indemnity. Our position: mutual cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000; Excluded Claims carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement; and confirmation that our payment obligations are not damages for cap purposes.

2. **§ 13.5 — termination fees deemed liquidated damages payable by us (high).** The deeming language fails the fallback three-month limit and approaches walk-away territory, and the fees are carved out of the cap. Minimal cure: strike the deeming language in the second sentence and confirm that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer, leaving the neutral first-sentence recital intact.

3. **§ 11.1 read with § 13.5 — combined exit cost (high, on the numbers).** An eight-year Term, a full year's notice and a fee calculated on the Monthly Base Fee for every remaining month, expressly outside the § 13.4 cap, is not an exit we can rely on. Whatever we settle on notice and fee, the fee must sit inside the cap and must not be characterised as liquidated damages.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Manual rework of the three unverified items — before any markup leaves the building.**
   - *Exclusivity (§ EXCLUSIVITY):* the automated review failed and produced no conclusion. Re-run manually, with particular attention to § 18.4 (M&I's right to bid) and § 10.3(A) (bundled-Services commitment), which are adjacent but were assessed under other rules.
   - *Termination for convenience:* the drafted proposal took us to the preferred position (30 days' notice, no fee, pro-rata refund, removal of M&I's § 10.2 withdrawal right) because the fallback check could not run — there is no M&I convenience-termination provision to restrict. Re-scope by hand to a defensible ask.
   - *Insurance:* re-draft the added E&O ($2,000,000) and cyber/privacy ($5,000,000) limbs and the CGL limits ($1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate) as new items 5 and 6 of § 14.1.
2. **Issue the verified redlines** for LOL-CAP, LD, ASSIGN, NOSOLICIT, TRANSITION, IP and MINCOMMIT, each with a short "[Playbook]" rationale and the fallback offered where we have one.
3. **Sequence the negotiation around the liability package.** Present § 13.4 and § 13.5 together with the § 11.1 exit fee as a single commercial issue; conceding the cap while leaving the liquidated-damages deeming in place would leave the exposure substantially unchanged.
4. **Confirm the commercial inputs** we do not hold: the Monthly Base Fee and the Termination for Convenience / for Cause Fee percentages, so we can size the exit exposure and the MINCOMMIT true-up before we trade.
5. **Do not open** the indemnity, licence, warranty, audit, governing law, MFN, renewal or non-compete provisions. Each is compliant and several are better than our preferred position; reopening them invites erosion. If Article 23 is reopened for another reason, we would add perpetual survival of the source-code licence once the then-current licence fees are paid.
"}
